messages.subject: Frequency distributions
parts:
I'm trying to set up a plot which will show the following:
On the Y axis I want to have my 3 genotypes (a, ab, b), and then I
wanted to have these further subdivided into 5 groups which correspond
to an ordinal trait (0,1,2,3,4).
Then on the Y axis I wanted to have frequency.
This way I could see if the usually normal distribution was being
skewed at any given genotype.
Any pointers on how to do this using R?

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: Frequency distributions
parts:
You can use the function plot.pxg() to look at the phenotype
as a function of the genotype at a marker or markers.

Alternatively, you could look at the contingency table. You'd
have to get access to the relevant bits in the cross object,
or read in the data in the more usual matrix form and work with
it directly.

If I had a cross called "mycross" and I wanted to look at a table
of the genotype of marker "D13Mit90" against the 3rd phenotype,
I could do the following:

g <- pull.geno(mycross)[,"D13Mit90"]
y <- mycross$pheno[,3]

table(y, g)

For an intercross, the genotypes in g get coded as 1,2,3 for
AA,AB,BB, respectively.

karl
